translation: For any arithmetic theory F whose axiom set is recursively enumerable, Def7 noncomputably defines an arithmetic sentence: the sentence saying that there is no proof of falsehood from the Δ₁-presented axiom set obtained from F by Craig’s trick. For any set K of arithmetic sentences and any arithmetic theory F, assuming F’s axiom set is recursively enumerable, Def8(K, F) holds exactly when both (1) K is the set of all sentences derivable from F and (2) the particular sentence Def7(F) belongs to K. Thus the membership required is in K, not necessarily in F’s axiom set. F is a parameter, not an existential witness, and neither the actual consistency of F nor the truth of the sentences in K is required.

divergences.description: Def7 uses the proof predicate for F.craig, not one for a particular original presentation of F. Since F.craig and F have exactly the same theorems, the sentence is true exactly when F is consistent. This is a faithful choice of consistency statement, not a presentation-independent formula. Its definition applies to any recursively enumerable arithmetic theory; sufficient strength and consistency matter for the unprovability theorem, not for forming the sentence.

K = F.theory captures the passage's antecedent, that the machine in fact has the same outputs as intuition. It does not capture knowing that this particular machine has those outputs. F is supplied externally, not identified by the knower. Even existentially quantifying F would not put the identification within the scope of knowledge, as required by the super strong mechanistic thesis.

The passage glosses “works correctly” as soundness: every output of the machine is true. Def7 says only that falsehood is not derivable. A consistent theory can prove false arithmetic sentences, so even genuine knowledge of Def7 would not amount to knowledge that the machine works correctly.

Given K = F.theory, the membership Def7 F ∈ K says exactly that F proves its Craig-presentation consistency sentence. Nothing requires K to be factive. For example, an inconsistent recursively enumerable F proves every sentence, including Def7 F, so Def8 holds with K = F.theory even though the consistency sentence is false. Such membership cannot by itself constitute knowledge.

judgement.summary: Def7 adequately renders arithmetic consistency. Def8 defines a condition of actual output equality and self-consistency provability, not the conjunction Gödel says is excluded: knowing the machine's identity and knowing its soundness.
